findings.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
findings.summary: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root . This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t This advisory is part of a group of advisories. For a complete list of the advisories and links to them, see Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of October 21, 2026, Security Advisories . In addition, for further documentation of improvements and fixes in Cisco Expressway Series see Cisco Expressway Series Security Hardening Release: October 2026 . Security Impact Rating: Critical CVE: CVE-2026-76466

findings.title: Agentic Attacks: In The Wild
findings.summary: Agentic offensive frameworks like ARTEX are driving a surge in cloud intrusions. Wiz Research shares cases from the wild, including both sides of one attack via the operator's leaked logs, an update on Black October, and the detections that catch these noisy, machine-speed attacks.

findings.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
findings.summary:
A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the popular binary-parser library that could allow an attacker who controls parser definitions to execute arbitrary code.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS score: 9.2 / 8.1), is a case of code injection impacting binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1.
